title.en: Rivers and natural regions of India

text.en:
Ravi traced the Ganga from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal on the map.
"Rivers connect our land," said his teacher.

India has Himalayan rivers like the Ganga, Yamuna and Brahmaputra, which flow all year, and peninsular rivers like the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, which depend mostly on rain.
Most peninsular rivers flow east into the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada and Tapi flow west into the Arabian Sea.
India's regions differ in landforms, soil, climate and natural vegetation, so people's lives differ too.
